content:
jen_support: Customer (AcmeAnalytics) - p99 TTFB regressions on streaming endpoints after last runtime deploy. Non-stream total times are fine. Raising here.

jen_support: Details: model=redwood-13b-v2, region=us-west-2, endpoint=/v1/generate, sample request_id=acme-req-2321

jen_support: They see p95~150ms (non-stream) but p99 streaming TTFB spikes to 3-6s intermittently. SLO is 500ms. Logs + curl repro below.

jen_support: curl (stream):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"summarize...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jen_support: curl (non-stream):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"summarize...","stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

matt_engineering: Can you paste a trace/span ID + any proxy logs around those timestamps? Also which commit/release rolled 03/09?

jen_support: Trace: span=span-0a1b2c3; proxy log snippet: "proxy-1 | flushing buffer delayed by 2200ms - client-side windowing". Attached stack:
```
[proxy] flush_delay=2200ms conn_id=9c3e
[runtime] kv-cache-hit=0 first_chunk_emit=3200ms
```

kyler_ml: Quick thought — looks like first-chunk emission delayed, not token generation. Possibly proxy/Nginx http2 windowing or client-side backpressure. Does the customer use HTTP/2 multiplexing or SSE?

jen_support: They confirm using HTTP/2 (gRPC-web client) from an on-prem proxy.

lucy_oncall: If proxy is coalescing small writes, TTFB would spike. We had a similar microburst issue when keepalive/flush settings changed in proxy config during 03/09 rollout. Can we reproduce by forcing immediate flush at gateway?

matt_engineering: Try adding header to bypass coalescing: `X-Stream-Force-Flush: 1` or set `Prefer: respond-mode=sync` to simulate non-stream. Kyler, does immediate-flush header exist in runtime?

kyler_ml: We added `x-flush-immediate` handling in runtime 2026-03-08 but it was gated behind a config flag that might not be enabled in the canary. If you pass `x-flush-immediate: 1` runtime will call flush after first chunk. Use this for repro.

jen_support: Customer tried `x-flush-immediate: 1` and reported p99 dropped from ~3.8s to ~420ms for first chunk. Recommending temporary app-level header workaround while we patch.

ravi_sre: I'll temporarily enable `runtime.flush-first-chunk=true` in canary gateway for us-west-2 to validate across traffic. Deploying now.

deploy-bot: rollout started: gateway-config/enable-flush-first-chunk -> canary (10%) - change id cfg-20260310-ff

ravi_sre: Canary shows improvement at 10% — p99 first-chunk reduced 85% in canary traces. No error increase.

matt_engineering: Root cause likely a subtle change in envoy/http2 write coalescing + our runtime not forcing flush on first chunk in some builds. We'll prepare a small runtime patch to always flush first chunk for HTTP/2 streaming, with a toggle.

kyler_ml: I'll add unit+integration tests simulating small-chunk HTTP/2 windowing and measure. Also add telemetry to emit `first_chunk_emit_ms` metric tagged by client-protocol.

jen_support: Customer ok with header workaround. Will tell them we'll patch and schedule a maintenance window if needed. :thumbsup:

lucy_oncall: Follow-ups: create perf test in perf-suite for HTTP/2 streaming, prod rollout runbook for enabling `runtime.flush-first-chunk` safely, and add docs snippet showing header workaround.

jen_support: I'll file the customer update and document repro steps. Thanks all — keeping this thread open until patch lands.
